House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries speaks at the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee headquarters on November 4 [Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images/AFP]By Al Jazeera StaffPublished On 9 Nov 20269 Nov 2026
United States House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has thrown his support behind impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, as the Democratic Party prepares to use its incoming congressional majorities to probe President Donald Trump’s administration.
In a Sunday appearance on the Television show This Week with George Stephanopoulos, Jeffries weighed in on the upcoming impeachment resolution, anticipated for the coming days.

“I’m a hard yes on the Hegseth resolution,” Jeffries said. “The so-called secretary of defence has abused his power, undermined our national security, and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran.”
The impeachment resolution has been spearheaded by outgoing Republican Representative Thomas Massie of Kentucky, a vocal critic of the US-Israel war on Iran.
“Pete Hegseth has got to go,” Jeffries added. “I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution.”
Investigating ‘unprecedented corruption’
Jeffries is poised to become the next speaker in the House of Representatives after Democrats notched a historic victory in the November 3 midterm elections.
Both the House and the Senate flipped into Democratic control, with the left-wing party making some of its biggest gains in the lower chamber in more than half a century.

The mayor of the Mexican border town of Rio Bravo has been found alive after being abducted in the violence-ridden Zacatecas state in northern Mexico.
Federal officials said Miguel Angel Almaraz was released by his captors on Sunday, hours after being taken to the city of Zacatecas.

Bavarian State Parliament President Ilse Aigner arrives at the Christian Social Union (CSU) party congress in Munich in October 2026 [AFP]By AFP, DPA and ReutersPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz will nominate Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner for Germany’s next president, which would make her the country’s first female head of state.
Merz made the announcement at a dinner for leaders of his centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party on Sunday.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Hoax or bomb threats? What we know about flight disruptions across Europelist 2 of 3Palantir harvests battlefield data that Ukraine pays for ‘with blood’list 3 of 3UK jailing of Indian sailor over Russia sanctions sets off ‘perfect storm’end of list
Aigner, speaker of the Bavarian state parliament, belongs to the Christian Social Union (CSU), the Bavarian sister party of the CDU.
If her nomination is confirmed at a CDU and CSU meeting on Monday, she would almost certainly be formally elected.
According to German political practice, coalition parties must agree on a common candidate. The governing coalition is made up of the CDU, the CSU and the Social Democratic Party (SPD).
The SPD has frequently voiced its support for Aigner as president.
The German president is elected by the Federal Convention, convened solely to choose the president. It will decide on incumbent Frank-Walter Steinmeier’s successor on January 30.
Steinmeier, a Social Democrat, took office in 2017, and will reach the limit of two five-year terms in March 2027.
Germany’s president holds a largely ceremonial position, signing legislation into law and formally appointing ministers.

Pope Leo XIV and Argentina's President Javier Milei take part in a welcome ceremony at Aeroparque Jorge Newbery International airport in Buenos Aires on November 8, 2026 [AFP]By AFP and ReutersPublished On 8 Nov 20268 Nov 2026
Argentinian President Javier Milei has welcomed the head of the Catholic Church, Pope Leo XIV, upon his arrival at Jorge Newbery airport near Buenos Aires.
Milei and his sister, presidential secretary Karina Milei, greeted the pope on Sunday amid tensions between the government and Argentina’s Catholic Church over austerity measures.
Recommended Stories list of 3 itemslist 1 of 3Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US general electionlist 2 of 3Pope Leo XIV arrives for South American tour after cancer surgerylist 3 of 3Pope Leo XIV delivers homily to thousands in Uruguayend of list
Prior to his arrival, the pope spent three days in Uruguay, the first stop on his tour of Latin America.
He is the first pontiff to visit Argentina in nearly four decades, since John Paul II’s trip in 1987.
“Without a doubt, it gives us great joy that this pope is visiting us,” said Jorge Silanes, religious director at the Pequeno Cottolengo Don Orione, a home for people with disabilities in the Buenos Aires province.
In Argentina, Pope Leo’s schedule includes attending a welcome ceremony at Plaza San Martin and a meeting with Milei at the Casa Rosada, the official presidential palace.
But the pontiff’s visit comes amid shrinking membership in the Catholic Church in Latin America, as well as a sometimes fractious relationship with politicians like Milei.
Catholics comprise the largest religious group in Latin America, with as many as 425 million people identifying with the church.

United States-based chipmaker Nvidia is investigating its chief executive officer, billionaire Jensen Huang, after he confirmed he had an intimate relationship with a woman accused of working for Chinese intelligence.
In an announcement on Sunday, Nvidia said the probe would be conducted by a “committee of independent directors” with outside counsel.

“While the board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the board’s inquiry will examine all available information,” Nvidia’s board of directors said.
It said the board continued to have “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team”. Huang will continue to lead Nvidia during the probe.
The investigation follows a report in The New York Times last month that Jensen may have been the target of a Chinese espionage plot.
China and the US have been in competition to dominate key tech sectors like artificial intelligence (AI).
Amid the AI boom, Nvidia has seen demand for its chips and programming interfaces explode, resulting in the company being valued in the trillions of dollars.
For years, the US has sought to restrict the export of advanced chips to China, fearing the Asian superpower could gain an edge over its technology and military sectors.

Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) chief executive Dana White is set to meet United States President Donald Trump on Monday, after the Republican leader jokingly raised the prospect of him becoming the next White House press secretary.
Trump announced the offer on Saturday, days after his Republican Party suffered record losses in midterm elections. In a post on Truth Social, the president praised White as “a violent Fighter and Warrior” who would bring along leading UFC fighters as “assistants” to “defend us against the Lunatic Left”.

While Trump has since clarified that he was “kidding”, the post revived scrutiny of the two men’s relationship.
In a news conference on Saturday, White confirmed he would soon travel to Washington, DC, to meet with Trump. He also appeared to brush aside the press secretary gig, citing his existing workload.
“I got a lot of jobs already,” White, a Trump ally and donor, said. “We have a meeting on Monday, so I’m sure I’ll have more to talk about after that.”
As Trump left West Palm Beach, Florida, on Sunday, he too clarified that the job offer was a joke.
